terra.problem: The text says a very large assembly gathered, not that the whole neighborhood showed up.
Men, women and children being present does not establish that the assembly included people other than Levites.
Shecaniah promises support, but the text does not say anyone promises to stay or that nobody is packing a bag.
The text says they took the oath, but that does not establish whether they mumbled.
The text says Ezra ate and drank nothing; it does not say there was no table.
The explanation is flat, and the claim that forty days would be a long road is confusing.
The text does not say the deadline is why everybody makes it, or that every exile appears.
The explanation repeats the consequence without adding much personality or insight.
The text says the people trembled regarding the matter, but their being nervous is an unmarked guess about their feelings.
The explanation repeats that it is raining in a flat, generic way.
The proposed process involves leaders, elders and judges, but the text does not say it is open or that nothing is handled privately at home.
The text does not establish whether the rainy season has ended when the work begins.
The text does not say the elders and judges know the local people.
The plan says the judges come with the elders; it does not say they sit beside them.
The text does not say God's anger is the thing that matters most to the assembly; that assigns them an unstated priority.
The text identifies the men Ezra selects as family heads, but it does not say none of them are singers.
